why: Doc quote is VERBATIM (interactive-mode.md line 288, third sentence of a four-sentence bullet; the fourth sentence adds the pre-2.1.218 Ctrl+B carve-out and does not reverse it). The IDENTIFIER half of the finding is true: no NESSY_/CLAUDE_ SUBAGENT_BG_SHELL_MAX_MS and no *_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP exists, `grep -rain` over packages/*/src apps/*/src returns nothing, no memory-pressure handler is registered, and process-supervisor.ts:215 sets `deadlineAt = request.persistent ? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER : Date.now() + request.timeoutMs` while moveToBackground (:409-412) lifts an already-running shell's deadline to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so a backgrounded shell genuinely has no wall-clock cap. But the finding's stated CONSEQUENCE -- 'a subagent's runaway shell can outlive the session indefinitely' -- is FALSE, and it is the exact recurring shape AGENTS.md warns about: the identifier is unwired, the consequence is already handled one layer up. Background shells are owned by a session key in the ProcessSupervisor store and every teardown path hard-drains them with a strict residual check that THROWS: ProcessSupervisor.drainSession (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:606-617) stops every running handle and raises ProcessSessionDrainError on any residual; disposeManagedAgentRuntime -- the ordinary session-end path (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:9594, drain at :9647) -- calls it; strictDrainPiSessionOwned re-checks and pushes `pi-session-process-residual:<handle>` (:9556-9559) into an AggregateError (:9567); the non-Pi path kills every backgroundShellCommands handle and throws `session-shell-owner-residual` (:9479-9486); and workspace-drain-participant.ts:58,:167 drains on workspace teardown. For the SUBAGENT case specifically the fork is tighter than the claim, not looser: a child session's stop drains the child's OWN session key and rejects leftovers -- SessionManager.ts:10698-10707, `drainSession(record.childSessionKey)` then `child-session-process-residual:<agentId>` if anything is still running/lost -- and every spawned subagent already carries a default 30-minute wall-clock deadline (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts:607, `deadlineAt: Date.now() + (cfg.timeoutMs ?? 30 * 60_000)`), enforced at SessionManager.ts:9968-9985 where expiry calls cancelProcessing on the child. So the default bound on a subagent-owned background shell here is 30 minutes to the subagent run plus a strict drain, against Claude's 60 minutes -- a different mechanism, not an absent one. Two secondary citation defects: background-task-settings.ts maps FOUR Claude env names (:9-:12 -- DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS, MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS, AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS, FORK_SUBAGENT), not 'only the off switch'; and pi-agent.ts:1783 is the closing line of the disableWorkflows comment -- the bash_background reference is at :1787-:1790, and the tool itself is defined in packages/pi-agent-server/src/tools/background-bash.ts:32 and registered via harness-tool-descriptor.ts:249. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3, and not a de-brand/product difference.
correctedState: Narrower and non-leaking. TRUE: Nessy has no env-configurable per-shell wall-clock cap (no NESSY_SUBAGENT_BG_SHELL_MAX_MS) and no OS memory-pressure reap (no NESSY_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP, no pressure handler anywhere); a shell moved to the background gets deadlineAt = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (process-supervisor.ts:215, :409-412) and so runs unbounded for as long as its owning session lives. FALSE: it cannot outlive the session. Background shells are session-key-owned and hard-drained at teardown by ProcessSupervisor.drainSession (process-supervisor.ts:606-617), which throws ProcessSessionDrainError on any residual; the drain is wired into ordinary session dispose (SessionManager.ts:9647), the strict Pi drain's residual check (:9556-9567), the non-Pi shell kill loop (:9479-9486) and workspace drain (workspace-drain-participant.ts:167). A subagent-owned shell is bounded twice over: the child session's stop drains its own key and rejects leftovers with child-session-process-residual (SessionManager.ts:10698-10707), and every subagent already runs under a default 30-minute deadline (spawner.ts:607, enforced SessionManager.ts:9968-9985) -- half Claude's documented 60-minute shell cap. The real residual gap is the missing knobs and the missing idle-session memory-pressure reap, not an unbounded process leak.
